title: Python: errors and exit codes
summary: Read a traceback from the bottom, catch only the error you expect, and tell the shell when a script failed.

text: When Python stops on an error, it prints a traceback. Read it from the bottom.
- The last line names the kind of error, and why.
- Above it, the chain of calls, the newest last, each with its file and line.
- Start at the lowest line that is in your own file.
- Python 3.11 and newer also draw ^^^ under the part that failed.
try runs code that may fail; except catches one kind of error and decides what to do: here, no settings file means the default settings.
- Name the error you expect: FileNotFoundError, KeyError, ValueError.
- ✘ A bare except: catches everything, even your typos and Ctrl+C: bugs hide behind it.
- An error you didn't expect should stop the script, loudly.
A script that fails must say so to whoever runs it: you, cron, a CI job.
- The message goes to stderr (file=sys.stderr), not into the output.
- OSError catches every way opening can fail: missing file, no permission, a folder.
- sys.exit(1) ends with status 1: the shell's && and if see the failure.
- An error nobody catches also ends with status 1, and a traceback. Catching it only to print 0 hides it.
